q: 1. The type of projection in which the surface are equally foreshortened is
explain: In isometric projection all three principal edges/axes of an object are foreshortened equally (by the same isometric ratio, ~0.816), unlike oblique or other projections where foreshortening differs by direction.

q: 2. In comparison to an isometric projection, the appearance of an isometric view is
explain: An isometric projection uses the reduced isometric scale (~0.816 of true length), while an isometric view/drawing is plotted using true (actual) lengths, making the isometric view appear larger than the true isometric projection.

q: 3. On isometric plane, a circle appears as
explain: Since isometric planes are inclined to the viewer, a circle lying on any isometric plane is foreshortened in one direction and appears as an ellipse.

q: 4. While making isometric projections the ellipse is preferably drawn by
explain: The four-center (approximate) method is the standard, quick way to construct isometric ellipses using arcs struck from four centers, giving a close approximation to the true ellipse.

q: 5. Isometric projection cannot be drawn by
explain: Isometric projections are commonly constructed using the box method, coordinate method, or offset method; the 'zone method' is not a recognized technique for isometric drawing (it is instead associated with development of surfaces, e.g., sphere development).

q: 6. A sphere in isometric projection appears as a circle of diameter
options: equal to the diameter of sphere
greater than the diameter of sphere
explain: In isometric projection (using the true isometric scale), a sphere projects as a circle whose diameter equals the sphere's actual diameter, since the same foreshortening ratio applies equally in every direction on a sphere.

q: 7. Projection of an object shown by three views is known as
explain: Multiview (orthographic) projection represents an object using multiple related views (typically front, top, and side) obtained by projecting perpendicularly onto mutually perpendicular planes.

q: 8. In orthographic projection, the elevation is obtained on a plane called
explain: The elevation (front view) of an object is obtained by projecting it onto the Vertical Plane (VP).

q: 9. In multiview projections, the XY line is also known as
explain: The XY line, which represents the intersection of the horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP), is commonly called the reference line.

q: 10. In first angle projection method, the relative positions of the object, plane and observers are
options: may be placed in any order
explain: In first angle projection, the sequence is Observer → Object → Plane of Projection, so the object lies between the observer and the plane.

q: 11. In first angle projection system, the right hand side view of an object is drawn
explain: In first-angle projection, each view is projected onto the plane behind the object and then folded into position, which places the right-side view on the left of the front view (elevation).

q: 12. If the front view of an object exhibits width and height, then what dimensions of an object are exhibited by a right side view?
explain: The front view shows width and height; the side view, being a projection along the width direction, shows the depth (length) and height of the object.

q: 13. For orthographic projections, B.I.S. recommends the following
explain: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS/IS codes) recommends first angle projection as the standard method for orthographic drawings in India.

q: 14. The recommended symbol for indicating the angle of projection shows two views of the frustum of a
explain: The standard projection symbol (as per BIS/ISO) is drawn using two views of a truncated cone (frustum of a cone), distinguishing first-angle from third-angle projection by the arrangement of the circle and its projection.

q: 15. The line joining the front and top views of a point is called
explain: The vertical line connecting the front view (elevation) and the top view (plan) of a point, perpendicular to the XY line, is called a projector.

q: 16. A point lying in the HP, has its top view above XY line. Its front view will be
explain: A point lying exactly in the Horizontal Plane (HP) has zero distance above VP, so its front view always lies on the XY (reference) line, regardless of where the top view is.

q: 17. A point whose elevation and plan are above XY, is situated in
explain: If both the front view (above XY, meaning in front of VP is reversed logic) and top view lie above the XY line, the point lies in the second dihedral angle (above HP and behind VP).

q: 18. In which of the following projection, the observer is at finite distance from the object?
explain: In perspective projection, the observer's eye (station point) is at a finite distance from the object, causing convergence of projectors to vanishing points, unlike orthographic/isometric/oblique projections which assume the observer is at infinity (parallel projectors).

q: 19. When the picture plane coincide with the object, the perspective of the object will be of its
explain: If the picture plane passes through the object itself, the perspective projection of that portion coincides with the object, so it appears at its actual (same) size.

q: 20. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
explain: First angle projection places the object between the observer's eye and the plane of projection (Observer → Object → Plane).

q: 21. The locus of a point is a ............. when in moves in a plane in such a way that its distance ............. a fixed line is always a constant.
explain: A point that maintains a constant perpendicular distance from a fixed straight line traces another straight line parallel to it.

q: 22. Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (Computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD perspective transformations rely on vector analysis to compute projections of 3D coordinates onto the picture plane.

q: 23. The ratio of the shortest distance from the focus to the shortest distance from the directrix is called
explain: Eccentricity is defined as the ratio of the distance of a point on a conic from the focus to its distance from the directrix; this ratio determines whether the conic is an ellipse, parabola, or hyperbola.

q: 24. Normally perspective projection is used by .............
explain: Perspective drawings, because they give a realistic, eye-view appearance of a finished project, are commonly used by manufacturers and marketers for promotional/presentation purposes.

q: 25. The nature of surface of sphere is .............
explain: A sphere's surface is curved in two independent directions simultaneously (both meridian and latitude directions), making it a doubly curved surface, unlike a cylinder or cone which are singly curved.

q: 26. If a semicircular thin sheet is folded to form a cone, then the front view of the cone appears as .............
explain: A semicircular development folded into a cone (where the semicircle's radius becomes the cone's slant height) produces a cone whose front view is an equilateral triangle, a special geometric relationship between the semicircle and the resulting cone's proportions.

q: 27. The intersection of a cone by a plane results in .............
explain: By definition, curves obtained by intersecting a cone with a plane (circle, ellipse, parabola, hyperbola, triangle) are collectively called conic sections.

q: 28. The curve of intersection of any solid with a line is .............
explain: A line, being one-dimensional, intersects the surface of a solid at discrete points (entry/exit points), not along a line or loop.

q: 29. When a cylinder penetrates into a vertical cone with their axes parallel to each other, the top view of the curve of intersection is .............
explain: When the penetrating cylinder's axis is parallel (coincident in direction) with the cone's vertical axis, the intersection curve, seen in the top view, projects as a circle.

q: 30. When a vertical cylinder is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder, the top view of the curve of intersection is .............
explain: The intersection of a vertical cylinder with a horizontal cylinder of different diameter produces a curve that, in the top view, appears as an elliptical arc.

q: 31. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection (which includes isometric, dimetric, and trimetric) is a category of orthographic (parallel) projection in which the object is tilted relative to the projection plane to show multiple faces at once.

q: 32. In the cabinet projection, an angle at which the projectors meet the plane of projection is .............
explain: Cabinet projection is an oblique projection drawn with receding lines at 30° (some texts use 45°) to reduce distortion, while depth is drawn at half scale; per this reference the receiving angle is taken as 30°.

q: 33. Bisecting a line means, divide a line into..... equal part.
explain: To 'bisect' literally means to cut into two equal portions.

q: 34. While making cavalier projections the ellipse is preferably drawn by .............
explain: In cavalier (and other oblique) projections, circular features on the receding faces are typically constructed using the oblong (rectangle-based) method to plot the true elliptical shape.

q: 35. The angle between two perpendicular line is
explain: Perpendicular lines are defined as lines that intersect at a right angle ($90^{\circ}$).

q: 36. One plane projection is
explain: Both axonometric and oblique projections are pictorial projections formed on a single plane, unlike multi-view orthographic projection.

q: 37. The angle between two horizontal line is
explain: Two parallel horizontal lines have a $0^{\circ}$ angle between them, while a single continuous horizontal line represents a $180^{\circ}$ straight angle.

q: 38. The point of intersection of co-ordinate axis is called
explain: The point where the x, y (and z) axes meet is by definition called the origin.

q: 39. Isometric projection, all distances are approximately this percentage of their size
explain: The isometric reduction factor of 0.815 corresponds to roughly 80% of the true size.

q: 40. In case of diametric projection
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: In dimetric projection two of the three axes make equal angles with the picture plane (are equally inclined), while the third differs.

q: 41. The angle between isometric axes is
explain: In isometric projection, the three principal axes are spaced equally at $120^{\circ}$ to each other.

q: 42. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is
explain: Due to the tilt of the object in isometric projection, all lines are foreshortened to approximately 81.5% of their true length.

q: 43. In perspective drawing, the size of elements depend on .............
explain: In perspective projection, apparent size diminishes with increasing distance from the observer (station point), mimicking how the human eye perceives depth.

q: 44. In case of perspective projection, picture plane is placed
options: out side of eye towards eye
explain: The picture plane is the transparent 'window' situated between the observer's eye and the object being viewed.

q: 45. Perspective projection is used to represent
explain: Perspective mimics how the human eye sees the world, with distant objects appearing smaller, providing a naturalistic 3D view.

q: 46. Normally perspective projection is used by ....... to represent the object
explain: Manufacturers and architects use perspective for marketing and presentations because it is easy for non-technical clients to understand.

q: 47. In isometric projection, the receding lines are drawn with the horizontal at .............
explain: In standard isometric projection, the two receding (isometric) axes are drawn at 30° to the horizontal, with the third axis vertical, giving the characteristic isometric appearance.

q: 48. Picture plane is
explain: The theoretical picture plane must be transparent so the projectors from the object can pass through it to the eye.

q: 49. In orthographic projection, the line of sight and the plane of projection are .............
explain: Orthographic projection is defined by projectors (lines of sight) that are perpendicular to the plane of projection, producing a true, undistorted view of the surface facing that plane.

q: 50. The plane on which perspective is formed is called:
explain: The image (perspective) is mathematically projected onto the Picture Plane (PP).
